name: ForEachLoop
caption: Loop Over Elements

edges.rules: Exactly one edge with value "for-each". Its steps are the loop body and run once per item. When the collection is empty, the body is skipped and the flow continues after the loop.

configuration.description: Exactly one SmartField placeholder, written '{{name}}', that points to an array output (for example a find-records step's '{{<slug>_results}}'), a collection, or a record reference/iterator such as a dotted relation '{{trigger_Rec.SalesLines}}' (SalesLines must be a reference definition in the flow's smartFieldDefs). Bare names without braces are rejected. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed. The selector is read in its raw, unsubstituted form at runtime.

outputs.name: items
outputs.when: always; emitted as {type:'reference', tableNo:<table of the records>} instead when the selector resolves to a record reference

outputs.name: currentItem
outputs.when: always; emitted as {type:'reference', tableNo:<table of the records>} instead when the selector resolves to a record reference

rules.check: configuration.selector must be non-empty (required field in the configuration dialog)
rules.message: Please fill in the highlighted fields.

rules.check: configuration.selector, trimmed, must start with '{{', end with '}}' and contain a non-empty name. Checked on the raw selector each time the step runs.
rules.message: The selector '%1' must use the SmartField placeholder notation (e.g. '{{name}}'). Bare selector names are no longer accepted – open the SmartField picker on the For Each step config to insert a valid placeholder.

rules.check: On the first pass the selector must resolve to an array (indexed entries name[0], name[1], ...), an iterable record reference, or an empty collection. A plain {{<slug>_<output>}} name that does not exist at all, or exists but is blank, counts as an empty collection. A scalar with content, or a dotted path that does not resolve to records, fails.
rules.message: The provided selector '%1' does not resolve to an array or iterable reference.

notes: Iteration is 1-based. 'iteration' = current pass (1..total), 'total' = number of items, 'currentItem' = items[iteration-1]. 'items' is stored as zero-based entries items[0..total-1].
The items are collected once, on the first pass, so changes the loop body makes to the source do not change the set being iterated.
There is no iteration cap on this step. The loop runs exactly 'total' times.

An empty collection is not an error: the body is skipped and the flow continues after the loop. For a plain {{<slug>_<output>}} selector this includes a name that does not exist at run time (a collection nothing was added to, but also a typo in the output name) and a blank output such as a Parser match that found nothing. Check selector names carefully; a typo silently skips the loop.
When an array output is also a record reference (e.g. find-records results), the array path is preferred, so each array entry becomes one item.
For a record reference that is not an array, all records in the reference's current filter view are iterated.

outputs[]: the editor emits items/currentItem as {type:'reference', tableNo:N} when the selector resolves to a record reference, otherwise as {type:'value'}. Hand-written JSON should do the same so downstream steps can bind record fields of currentItem.
The step also emits a runtime-only 'result' value ('for-each' while there are items). This is what the engine routes on. It is not declared in outputs[].

Outputs of steps INSIDE the loop body are deleted each time control returns to the loop step and after the loop finishes. Reference them only inside the body; collect results into a collection step if you need them later.
